analysis: Examined two files. (1) ClusterPlacementFlow.swift: the only change (head lines 289-294) appends explanatory text to the plan output when the layout's tensor-parallel family chooses the fastest mode and tensor parallel is admissible. It adds a static message plus ClusterModelFeaturePolicy.modeFeatureNote(capability), which is capability-derived text. This is local, human-readable narration only. It does not alter policy.modes, admission, grants, leader selection, setup synthesis, or any key, attestation or authorization path. The surrounding unchanged planning logic stays on the same gates: capability/layout hash match, admittedCuts subset check, ClusterPairServingGrants.plannable, and the debug-only bench caps. I found no new data exposure, since the note is derived from capability, not from consumer prompts. (2) InstalledBatchLanesCheck.swift: test-only additions. They assert that Gemma tensor parallel defaults to 1 lane, accepts 2/4/8 by explicit override, retires lanes alone, forwards the adapter arithmetic environment (MLX_GATHER_QMM_EXPERT_SLICES=trust, MLX_GEMMA4_FUSED_WEIGHTED_UNSORT=1), rejects malformed overrides, and captures logprobs for TP but not for pipeline. These strengthen coverage of the owner-environment sanitization boundary (the DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES and unrelated-variable non-forwarding checks remain in base). The tests do not change production code. The production behavior that makes Gemma TP work (defaultBatchLanes, DistributedResidentExecutionProfile, nativeEnvironment) is not in this batch's supplied units. Whether the Gemma TP support in those unseen sources, such as lane retirement and the 'trust' expert-slice environment, is safe cannot be verified here, so a later pass should check it. No threat-model regression is identified in the supplied units, and none of the cache threat (T-041) paths are touched.
